text:
maya_g: Heads-up, ran a small bring-up sweep for the new 7B reranker on MS MARCO + internal logs. Seeing an unexpected MRR drop when we concat title+body vs body-only. Starting a thread to capture quick notes and next steps.

kevin_r: Which runtime/config? quantized or FP16 baseline? :thinking:

maya_g: FP16 baseline, plus Q4_0 quant for perf experiments. The drop shows up in FP16 too, so not purely quant noise.

sana: Can you paste the eval snapshot / metrics?

maya_g: Sure — short table from the checkpoint run (eval split small pilot):

```
Dataset      | Format      | NDCG@10 | MRR@10
MSMARCO      | title+body  | 0.587   | 0.412
MSMARCO      | body-only   | 0.613   | 0.439
InternalLogs | title+body  | 0.624   | 0.455
InternalLogs | body-only   | 0.619   | 0.451
```

thomas_m: Huh — title+body is worse on MSMARCO but slightly better on internal logs. Could be dataset label granularity or truncation/windowing.

maya_g: I tried toggling `doc_concat_order=title_first` vs `body_first` — no large change. However, when I stripped HTML and normalized punctuation in titles, title+body improved on MS MARCO.

kevin_r: Maybe tokenization mismatch? Titles are short and often have punctuation (colons, pipes). Did you try lowercasing vs cased tokenization?

maya_g: Lowercasing helped for MSMARCO title+body: MRR .412 -> .426, still below body-only.

sana: Also check label mapping — MSMARCO qrels are passage-level. Concatenating title+body could push the relevant passage position and change how the reranker interprets relevance.

maya_g: Good point. I ran a sliding-window chunking experiment (max_tokens=512) and scored best chunk with reranker instead of scoring full concat. That moved title+body MRR up to .434 on MSMARCO. So position/spans matter.

thomas_m: For quantization: do you see score compression / loss of dynamic range? Could affect tie-breaking in top ranks.

maya_g: Q4 produced slightly noisier logits. A simple temperature calibration on logits (fit temp on small heldout set) helped; applying temp=0.95 reduced rank regressions in Q4 runs.

eval-bot: queued eval job #1128: full grid (formats x quant levels x tokenization) running overnight. Results will land in dataset job #1129.

kevin_r: Nice. Let's standardize preprocessing: strip HTML, collapse whitespace, remove nav/boilerplate blocks, normalize punctuation, and include an explicit separator token between title/body (e.g., `[TIT]` or `</s>`). Can we add that to the eval harness?

maya_g: I'll open a tiny PR with the preprocessing script + notebook with ablations. Also propose we test `concat-with-sep` vs `concat-no-sep` and `best-chunk` vs `full-doc` as controlled factors in the harness.

sana: And include dataset diversity: MS MARCO (passage-level), Natural Questions (doc-level), and a noisy web crawl subset to cover short vs long docs. We need to catch format-specific regressions.

thomas_m: Also add logging of score distributions per-format (mean, std, percentile) so we can detect compression after quantization. If the top-1 margin shrinks, that explains MRR dips.

kevin_r: Can we add CI guards? E.g., if a model flip causes >1% relative MRR drop on the canary holdout we fail the rollout.

maya_g: Yep — plan: add a canary eval (10k holdout queries) measured for NDCG@10 and MRR@10, plus automated temp-calibration for quantized builds. I'll include the regression threshold and a small script to compute relative delta.

kevin_r: :thumbsup: Also run latency checks on Dedicated to ensure batching still meets SLO with the chunking approach.

maya_g: Will do. For next steps: 1) PR with preprocessing + ablation notebook, 2) wait for eval-bot job #1128 full results, 3) add CI canary and score-distribution logging. I'll post PR link here when ready.

sana: Great. One more ask — capture exact tokenizer versions and model commit in the eval metadata so we can reproduce.

maya_g: Yep — adding tokenizer sha, model-commit, and eval-harness gitref to the job metadata. Will update thread with links.

thomas_m: Thanks. Keeping an eye. :eyes: 

maya_g: PR and results incoming.

kevin_r: Thanks everyone.
